NIPPERS — LEVER ASSISTED — END 
CUTTING — SPECIFICATION

Assembly Hand Tools Sectional Committee, PE 05 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Assembly Hand Tools Sectional Committee had been approved by the Production Engineering 
Division Council. 

Lever assisted end cutting nippers are used for cutting hard wires and are mostly used in engineer- 
ing industries. Other type of nippers used for wire cutting are given below for the reference of 
users and manufacturers: 

IS 4378 ( Part 1 ) : 1990 Nippers : Part 1 Diagonal cutting nippers ( second revision ) 

IS 4378 ( Part 2 ) : 1990 Nippers : Part 2 End cutting nippers ( second revision ) 

IS 12985 : 1990 Toggle lever assisted end cutting nippers 

IS 13887 : 1993 Nippers — Lever assisted — Diagonal cutting 

This standard is in conformity with the requirements given in ISO 5747-1984 'Pliers and nippers — 
Lever assisted side cutting pliers, end and diagonal cutting nippers — Dimensions' issued by 
the International Organization for Standardization ( ISO ). 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded 
off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The 
number of significant places retamed in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the 
specified value in this standard. 



IS 13888 : 1993 



Indian Standard 

NIPPERS — LEVER ASSISTED — END 
CUTTING — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

This standard covers the dimensions and other 
requirements for lever assisted end cutting 
nippers. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard: 



IS No. 
2615; 1989 



Title 

Technical supply conditions 
for pliers and nippers ( second 
revision ) 



IS No. Title 

11526; 1986 Nomenclature for pliers, 

pincers and nippers 

3 NOMENCLATURE 

For the purpose of this standard, the nomen- 
clature as given in IS 11526 : 1986 shall apply. 

4 DIMENSIONS 

4,1 The dimensions of lever assisted end cutting 
nippers shall be as given in Table 1.

5 HARDNESS 

Body 350 to 510 HV ( -^ 35 to 50 HRC ) 

Near cutting 510 to 700 HV { ^ 50 to 60 HRC) 
edges 

NOTE — For method of checking hardness, refer 
IS 2615 : 1989. 

6 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 

The material, manufacture, workmanship and 
finish, tests, preservation and packing and sam- 
pHng shall conform to IS 2615 : 1989. 

7 TESTS 

In addition to the tests specified in IS 2615 : 
1989, test laid down at 7.1 and 7.2 shall also 
be carried out. 

7.1 Handle Load Test 

The pliers shall be tested in accordance with 9.5 
of IS 2615 : 1989. The load (F) shall be as given 



in Table 2. The permanent set shall not exceed 
the values specified in Table 2. 

7.2 Hard Wire Cutting Test 

Pliers shall be tested in accordance with 9.1 of 
IS 2615 : 1989. The test wire diameter shall be 
as given in Table 2. 

8 DESIGNATION 

Lever assisted end cutting nippers shall be desig- 
nated with its commonly used name, nominal 
size and number of thi^s standard. 

Example: 

Lever Assisted End Cutting Nipper — 

IS 13888 — 160 

9 MARKING 

The pliers shall be marked with nominal size and 
the manufacturer's name, initials or the recog- 
nized trade-mark. The year of manufacture may 
also be marked if required by the purchaser.

standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
StcmduTds Act^ 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark 
on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been 
produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system 
of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and 
operated by th^ producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by 
BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under 
which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or 
producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards; 



Burean of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Aci^ 1986 to 
promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality 
certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced 
in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, 
in the course of implementing the standard, bf necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type 
or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director 
( Pubhcations ), BIS 

Rerision of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards 
are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaflBrmed when such review 
indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken 
up for revision- Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the 
latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of *BIS Handbook' and 'Standards 
Monthly Additions'. Comments on this Indian Standard may be sent to BIS giving the following 
reference:
